subject: Request: temporary SLA amendment for Aurora Metrics rollout
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Celia Ramos <celia.ramos@aurorametrics.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary SLA amendment for Aurora Metrics rollout

Hi Celia,

We have a production rollout planned for Aurora Metrics starting Tue 3/1 at 23:00 PT that will push a large backlog and real-time ingestion spike into our hosted inference tier for ~72 hours. Based on the modeled traffic (attached) we expect a 3–4x increase in P2 incident volume overnight for the first 48 hours.

To avoid noisy P2 escalations and to give engineering time to stabilize the deployment, we propose a short, targeted amendment to your Support Response SLA:

- Scope: P2 response window adjusted from 2 hours to 4 hours (P1 unchanged)
- Duration: 72 hours starting 2027-03-01 23:00 PT
- On-call coverage: dedicated standby rotation (one engineer on 30-min standby for high-severity alerts)
- Escalation path: standby -> Mina (on-call lead) -> Mateo -> Aurora exec contact

We also recommend keeping the automatic fallback routing engaged (we will route traffic to your dedicated pool and enable increased batching limits briefly). This is intended as a temporary operational waiver to reduce churn while the rollout completes.

Can you confirm whether Aurora can accept the temporary P2 window extension and standby arrangement? If so, Procurement can sign off and we will push an entry into the SLA amendment tracker and notify billing for any credit adjustments.

Attachments: aurora-rollout-plan.pdf, expected-nightly-traffic.csv

Thanks,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Mateo — appreciate the heads-up and the detail. A few quick questions before I confirm with Procurement:

1) Will Aurora receive any service credits if we accept the temporary extension? If yes, what is the formula?
2) Can you confirm that P1 response times and availability SLAs remain unchanged?
3) Who is the standby engineer and how will we be looped in when they escalate?

Procurement is looped on this thread (procurement@aurorametrics.com). We are time-sensitive here; please respond today if possible. I am copying our support ops so they have the fallback/routing details.

—Celia
Celia Ramos
Head of Platform Operations | Aurora Metrics
celia.ramos@aurorametrics.com

Hi Celia — answers inline:

1) Service credits: We are proposing a limited credit equal to 10% of monthly support fees for the billing period that includes the amendment window if any P2 incidents exceed the adjusted 4-hour window and are determined to be Redwood-attributable. If no breaches occur, no credits apply. The exact credit mechanics will be added to the amendment doc for Procurement to sign.

2) Correct — P1 response (30 minutes) and uptime/availability commitments are unchanged. This is specifically a temporary operational adjustment to P2 acknowledgement/initial-response only.

3) Standby plan: 
- Primary standby: Robin Patel (internal rotation; contact robin.patel@redwood.com, phone +1 415 555-0199) — will take first triage for elevated P2s overnight.
- On-call lead: Mina Haddad (mina.haddad@redwood.com) — escalation for any incidents that require cross-team fixes or rollbacks.

We will also create a shared Slack channel and provide direct bridge details. I have attached a small spreadsheet (standby-rotation.xlsx) showing the proposed 72-hour rota and the runbook snippet we'll use for triage.

If Aurora agrees to the proposed 72-hour window and standby rota, Procurement can countersign and we will log the amendment in SUP-1124 (JIRA) and notify Billing.

Cheers,
Mateo
